title: Xbox admits licensing failure that prevented disc games
seoTitle: Xbox admits licensing glitch that blocked disc games
subtitle: 20-hour outage raises debate about the digital future of games
excerpt: On July 30, 2026, Xbox faced a 20-hour outage caused by a licensing glitch that blocked disc usage, reigniting debates about the future of digital gaming.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
On July 30, 2026, Xbox's technology service was unavailable for approximately 20 hours, preventing some players from accessing their games via physical discs. The failure was attributed to a licensing problem that did not correctly verify user eligibility.

License failure blocks disc games

The outage occurred because the disc-based entitlement verification system did not work as intended. Platform chief technology officer Scott Van Vliet said the situation was \"unacceptable\" and that it should not have blocked access to the games.

Xbox chief technology officer's reaction

Van Vliet stated: \"We’re looking into reports that some players were unable to access games using discs as expected during the service interruption.\" He then added: \"Disc-based entitlement checks should not prevent players from accessing their games and this is by design.\"

Context of recent outages

The Xbox incident follows a parallel PlayStation Network outage that occurred on July 24, as well as another PlayStation interruption the previous Friday. Both episodes rekindled concerns about a future of exclusively digital games and about title ownership and licensing.

Developments in physical media policies

In June, Rockstar Games announced that physical copies of GTA 6 would include a code for digital download instead of a disc containing the game. Nintendo has also moved toward digital with its Game-Key Cards, which function as keys for download. Sony, meanwhile, revealed plans to stop releasing new PlayStation games on discs starting January 2028, keeping retail sales but only with digital codes.

Consumer and expert reactions

One commentator responded to Van Vliet’s post: \"I think this highlights how important it is to move towards truly consumers owning their digital games.\" He added: \"If consoles are going to become digital only, then issues like today cannot lock people out of their stuff.\" Scott Ross, co-founder of the Stop Killing Games movement, warned: \"The problem is the industry has a very poor reputation of disabling games once they end support.\" He also said: \"I don’t think the lack of a disc is the problem in itself, but rather it can be a symptom of a larger, very consumer-hostile practice.\" Jez Corden, executive editor of Windows Central, said Sony’s decision \"put digital rights under a microscope\" and that Xbox’s statement showed the company is \"sensitive of the discussions around digital rights and disc-based games right now\". Digital sales already represent the majority of game revenue, and the recent outages may encourage companies to rethink their strategies.

With information from BBC News.
